PullRequest.Title: Tyler leonhardt/quick access highlight fix
PullRequest.Body:
Just the "quotes" support from #131215 fixing the highlighting problem so typing:

`"26"` will actually highlight 2020-7-`26` and not `2`020-7-2`6`.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Static callers, exhaustive loops, cache behavior, history cap and full-candidate top selection prove the mechanism; duration and large-workspace prevalence are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Q*T CPU matrix-cell calculations and two temporary Q*T numeric arrays per target.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: O(U*Q*T) matrix work for U distinct uncached substring misses. U is at most 200 for history and can be thousands of fuzzy-filtered workspace paths; identical cached queries do not repeat scoring.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: UI-thread input latency and GC pressure in quick access, plus slower workspace search-result delivery.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Non-fuzzy substring misses returned NO_SCORE before constructing scoring matrices.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every eligible substring miss now builds both full scoring matrices, despite returning zero.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The deleted includes guard removes the early return before doScoreFuzzy; the replacement startsWith check is inside the exhaustive matrix loops.
Findings.Title: Keep the fast rejection for missing contiguous substrings
Findings.Impact: Typing a nonmatching history filter now builds unnecessary matrices on the UI thread. A quoted query that matches thousands of workspace paths only non-contiguously causes the same work across all those candidates before results return.
Findings.Evidence: doScoreFuzzy loops over all Q*T cells and writes two arrays even with zero scores. anythingQuickAccess.ts:456 uses false synchronously for history, capped at 200. Quoted queries also select false at fuzzyScorer.ts:465,507. Workspace filtering uses fuzzyContains (search.ts:557), allowing subsequence-only paths into rawSearchService.ts:256 scoring. topAsync examines all candidates, not just the 512 returned results. Cache hits avoid repeat comparator scoring, but each new item/query key incurs the work.
Findings.Recommendation: Restore the upfront includes rejection when non-contiguous matching is disabled, while retaining the new startsWith scoring gate for contiguous highlights.

Scenarios.Scenario: Typing in Quick Open with recently opened editors included
Scenarios.CriticalPath: picker.onDidChangeValue immediately invokes _getPicks, which synchronously runs getEditorHistoryPicks before starting the slow file/symbol searches or applying results. Matrix scoring therefore blocks the input handler and delays launching the slow branch.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 200 history entries, reduced to distinct scorer keys after resource eligibility checks and identical-label deduplication. Ordinary filters score labels only; path-containing filters can also score descriptions. Targets shorter than the query still reject early. Each query piece adds work until a piece fails.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded synchronous scoring with no debounce or yield on the history path. Later sort comparisons reuse the same scorer cache rather than rebuilding matrices for every comparison.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The scorer cache is reset for a normal picker session. It caches positive and zero scores by label, optional description, normalized query, piece count and matching flags. Repeated identical keys are warm; a newly typed normalized query is cold even when file-query caches are warm. The property rename preserves cache-key values and lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the unquoted history caller explicitly passes false, the removed substring guard formerly preceded allocation, and the remaining loops fill both full matrices even for misses.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: History is bounded at 200, so the duration depends on label/path lengths and query length. No measured input latency is available.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work regression, covered by the accepted finding: substring misses newly incur Q*T matrix work on the UI thread. History lookup, label creation and canHandleResource checks introduce no filesystem, subprocess, network or IPC operation on this scoring path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Filtering open-editor quick-access lists with quoted and unquoted queries
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The input handler synchronously creates editor entries, filters every entry with scoreItemFuzzy, sorts accepted entries and applies the list. No scoring work is off the UI critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: All editors supplied by the active-group or all-groups provider, potentially hundreds. Actual expensive scoring occurs once per distinct label/description/query cache key, not once per group duplicate or comparison. Each rejected label may be followed by a description-plus-label target.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous serial filter and sort on the UI thread. No limiter, async boundary or debounce is introduced or removed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cache resets on normal picker provision and is reused during the session. Both matching and nonmatching items are cached. Empty queries skip scoring. New normalized queries are cold; identical queries and sorting comparisons are warm.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: editorQuickAccess.ts:81 passes true, and fuzzyScorer.ts:465,507 turns that into false for quoted query pieces. The changed matrix path is directly reachable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Open-editor count and description lengths vary. The additional branch for ordinary fuzzy queries is not independently established as significant.
Scenarios.Verdict: Quoted substring misses have the same regression already reported; no duplicate finding. Unquoted fuzzy scoring retains its existing matrix scale. Filtering reads existing editor metadata and introduces no expensive boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Quick Open workspace-file results, including cold cache loading, warm searches and path probes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After synchronous history filtering, file picks await an absolute-path probe when applicable, then the main workspace search and relative-path probes concurrently. Search results must be filtered and scored before the top results are serialized and returned; the renderer then merges and scores picks. Background cache population uses maxResults=0 and skips comparator scoring.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check existence of each workspace folder before dispatching search providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: F logical exists calls in parallel per search request, where F is the number of workspace roots. Usually one request per filter; a multi-piece query hitting the result limit can issue a second sequential request. Cache loading also issues a request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-request folder checks and concurrency existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Folder checks precede provider dispatch, including when search results can subsequently use a warm cache.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate search extensions as needed and dispatch one grouped query per URI scheme, with local disk queries sent to the shared search service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Activation requests are grouped by distinct scheme, plus onSearch:file, with extension activation reuse. Search dispatch is per scheme group rather than per file; local disk search uses one IPC request per logical search. A multi-piece limit-hit fallback can add one sequential search.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical grouped dispatch, activation requests, cache keys and search-request counts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Activation and provider completion are awaited; additional matrix work delays result completion but does not add requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run ripgrep --files for each workspace root on an uncached disk search.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One ripgrep process per root for each cold enumeration, running roots concurrently. Cached result-prefix reuse does not enumerate again. The background full-file cache can serve later queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same subprocess cardinality, root concurrency and cache reuse; the diff changes scoring cost only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold enumeration completes before sorted results return. Cache population is background work; warm query scoring still lies on the result critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve an explicitly requested absolute or workspace-relative path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No probes without a path separator. At most one absolute-path resolve; for relative paths, up to F logical resolve calls, sequentially awaited, alongside the grouped search.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same path conditions, probe counts, ordering and serial relative-root loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Absolute resolution precedes normal file search; relative resolution is awaited with search before file picks can complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize/log the query and send selected search matches over the existing search channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Query metadata scales with roots and extra resources. Normally up to 512 results per foreground search are selected before transport; a sequential multi-piece fallback can supply another result set. Cached prefix candidates can be much larger than this transport limit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same query serialization, selected-result transport and batching; substring misses previously rejected before matrix construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: rawSearchService.sortResults finishes before selected matches are converted and emitted. The expensive matrices are built before this output cap is applied.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Let C be paths passing existing fuzzyContains filtering, potentially thousands in a large workspace, and U be their distinct label/description/query scorer keys. Quoted queries can pass this subsequence filter without matching any contiguous substring. The 512 output cap does not bound U because topAsync examines every candidate. Renderer inputs are selected file results plus optional symbol picks and relative-path results after resource exclusions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: File and optional symbol acquisition are parallel. Workspace scheme providers and ripgrep roots run concurrently; relative path probes are serial. Search-process topAsync scores serially and yields between 10000-candidate batches. Renderer top selection is synchronous. Comparator caching limits matrices to once per distinct item/query key.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: FileQueryCacheState can reuse a previous loaded cache while refreshing. rawSearchService joins cached result promises and filters prefix-compatible cached enumerations. Its scorer cache stores both zero and positive item scores per query key. A warm file-list cache therefore does not eliminate cold scoring for a new query. Cache-loading queries request zero results and do not score.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: fuzzyContains admits noncontiguous paths, quote preparation selects contiguous scoring, and topAsync checks all candidates before transport. The removed guard adds matrix work without changing any expensive boundary count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of subsequence-only matches and their path lengths is workload-dependent. No profiling measurements are available; exact provider-internal network operations are implementation-dependent and are not newly invoked by this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: Same accepted eager-work regression, materially visible as extra CPU/GC work and longer result latency for quoted substring misses. No separate boundary-fanout, concurrency or cache-lifecycle regression. Background cache population is not newly burdened with scoring.

Scenarios.Scenario: Optional workspace-symbol acquisition and merging into Quick Open; standalone symbol scoring
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SymbolsQuickAccessProvider delays requests by 200ms, awaits all registered workspace-symbol providers, filters their results with scoreFuzzy2, and returns picks. Quick Open awaits both files and symbols, then synchronously scores the combined collection before selecting 512 picks. Standalone symbol scoring uses the unchanged alternate scorer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request workspace symbols from registered providers; extension-backed providers use $provideWorkspaceSymbols and release their preceding result handle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per registered provider per issued delayed query, not per returned symbol. Extension-backed providers can add one release call when a previous result ID exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same provider request count, parallelism, delay, cancellation and preceding-result release.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider requests run concurrently and all complete before picks are merged. Their calls are unchanged; additional primary-scorer work happens afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transfer and revive symbol result DTOs from extension-backed providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Scales with the number of symbols returned by each provider; the provider may impose its own cap. One result set serves the complete provider query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same DTO data, result cardinality and revival work; the renamed prepared-query flag is not transported here.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Result transfer/revival precedes symbol filtering and final Quick Open merging.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P registered providers and their returned symbol collections. For merged Quick Open results, expensive primary scoring is once per distinct item/query cache key across selected file picks and eligible symbol picks before the overall 512 cap. Standalone symbol filtering uses existing scoreFuzzy2 and does not consume the renamed contiguous-match flag.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All P providers are requested concurrently after the delay, with no new global limiter or burst. File acquisition is parallel with symbol acquisition. Final top selection/scoring is serial synchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ThrottledDelayer coalesces pending input and checks cancellation before provider issuance. No new provider cache is introduced. Final Quick Open scoring uses the existing per-session item cache, including zero scores; new query keys miss it. Provider-owned caches are outside the inspected implementation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the inspected provider IPC, unchanged alternate scorer and changed merged primary-scorer reachability. Provider-specific external I/O is not established and is not attributed to the diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider count, returned symbol count, provider caches and provider-internal service/network costs vary and are unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independently introduced provider-boundary or standalone-symbol regression. Quoted misses during the existing combined-list primary scoring are covered by the single accepted finding; passing renamed query metadata to the alternate scorer does not increase its work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the full two-file inventory and all diff pages, tracing scorer callers, cache ownership, input scheduling, candidate selection and relevant search/provider boundaries. One medium-severity eager-work regression was accepted: deleting the contiguous-substring fast rejection newly builds full matrices for misses. No concrete performance regression fix requiring blame provenance was established. Review is static; exact durations and workload prevalence are unmeasured.
